Austin is called a "naive empiricist" because his account of law rests on an anachronistic model: he modelled law on a simple, historical type of legal system (sovereign commands backed by sanctions) that doesn't fit how modern legal systems work. Assuming this is John Austin, I can't verify the label's source myself, so this relies on the shared note that the answer is one of these two options. The other option, that he denies any link between law and morality, doesn't match the "naive empiricist" wording as well.

CONFIDENCE: 70
